newsitem.title: KENYA: Dollar demand adds pressure on Kenyan shilling.
newsitem.headline: Dollar demand adds pressure on Kenyan shilling.

text.p: Continued demand for the dollar put pressure on the Kenyan shilling, forcing it down marginally on Thursday, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.76 against the dollar from 55.74 on Wednesday, while on the pound, it was posted at 92.03 from 91.86.

Dealers said high import demand led to a further weakening of the shilling. "Demand from the oil sector continued to mount, while exporter sales dwindled, forcing the shilling to dip," a commercial dealer said.
"Dollar supply is not adequate, importers have cleared the money in the market," another dealer said.
Dealers said many importers had been stockpiling their orders waiting to take advantage of the new shilling levels.
"It seems many importers are placing orders at the current levels after realising that the dollar/shilling rate is reversing," a dealer said.
They also said they expect the shilling to depreciate further until demand from the oil companies was met. They, however, cast doubt on the shilling reaching the 56 level.
Liquidity in the money market eased as most banks put their money in treasury bills. Rates were quoted at 15-20 percent levels from 10-15 percent levels on Wednesday.
